text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Fifteen bandits are shot dead in a counter-offensive against bandits holed up in Suguta Valley in the northern Rift Valley area of Samburu where a district commissioner and two army officers were killed last Thursday.
- Following an incident where a man was stabbed on the head, ruling KANU party sub-branch elections in Changamwe, Coast province, are nullified.
- Human rights lawyer Mirugi Kiruki urges the commissioner of police to abide by the law and allow prisoners to receive food from relatives.
- James Orengo, deputy official leader of the opposition breaks his long silence with a stinging criticism of the Opposition leadership, dismissing elusive unity as "silly and stupid".
- Elders in the Mount Kenya region of Kirinyaga hold a "burnt offering" with sacrifice of lamb to God for rain.
- Government is urged to declare curfew in all bandit-prone areas.
- Thousands of Kenyans mark the year's last Sunday with prayers for peace, understanding and reconciliation.

- At least five international companies including three with an East African presence are claiming some $70 million from the United Nations for services and supplies provided to UN troops during the failed Somali operation.
- Uganda National Drug Authority closes down 200 drug shops while another 300 voluntarily stop operating after failing to meet the required standards over the last 12 months.
